name: The Standard, Miami
positioning: Adults-only spa hotel, officially The Standard Spa, Miami Beach, set in tropical gardens on Belle Isle, steps from South Beach
best_for: Adults who want a spa-focused stay close to South Beach
Travelers who enjoy hydrotherapy, bathing rituals and daily wellness classes

facts.text: The hotel is located on Belle Isle, steps away from South Beach.
Belle Isle, home of the hotel, was originally named Bull Island and is part of the Venetian Islands.
The Standard Spa, Miami Beach is for adults and describes itself as less a hotel and more a spa with guest rooms.
The hotel is set amidst tropical gardens.
The spa encourages the communal rituals of ancient bathing traditions.
The hotel runs a daily schedule of wellness and fitness classes and a workshop series with in-house staff and international teachers.
The gym has Peloton bikes, treadmills and free weights.
Guests may use the pool, spa and gym before check-in and after check-out.
The lobby hosts events such as talks, readings and pop-ups.
The shop sells surf and sun goods, from bikinis to bronzer to board shorts.
Lido Bayside serves global-inspired dining on the bay.
Belle is a dining spot exclusively for hotel guests and members.

highlights.text: An indoor and outdoor hydrotherapy playground is complimentary to hotel guests.
Spa facilities include a Turkish-style hammam, an aroma steam room, a sauna, an ice room, a Roman waterfall hot tub, an arctic plunge, treatment baths and an infinity pool.
Rooms feature private terraces, many with outdoor soaking tubs.
The hotel hosts retreats, lectures, classes, seminars and events led by local, national and international figures in health, fitness, spirituality, art and more.
Hotel guests get 15% off regular-priced admission to the Bass Museum of Art with their room key card, with a blackout during Miami Art Week.

considerations.text: The hotel is for adults, so it does not suit families travelling with children.
The pool and spa are shared with outside visitors: Monday to Thursday day passes and memberships give non-guests access.
WhataHotel notes the hotel is on the quieter bay side rather than the ocean beachfront.
